key_warnings: Leverage and margin debt are extremely dangerous in concentrated portfolios. The Leopold fund case study shows that 3-4x leverage can completely wipe out positions during rapid market corrections in volatile growth stocks. The Leopold fund was up 1,000% since inception and 270% year-to-date in May, but lost 67% in July when semiconductor names dropped 30-60% in weeks due to Kimi K3 and Chinese DUV machine news. Do not use excessive leverage.

Using weekly options on earnings reports or making leveraged bets on single events is gambling, not investing, regardless of research hours spent. Stock performance on earnings announcements is unpredictable and can move down even on good earnings. The Chris Camillo Amazon options bet and the Leopold fund liquidation demonstrate this risk. Macro events, geopolitical issues, and tweets can negate all research.

Good earnings reports do not guarantee positive stock movement. Google, SoFi, Meta, and Reddit all reported excellent quarters but experienced stock declines or sideways movement. Stock sentiment and price momentum matter more in the short term than fundamental business quality.

AI infrastructure capital expenditure ($1.4 trillion cumulative through 2028 for 120 gigawatts) carries significant ROIC uncertainty. Token pricing per million tokens is the key unknown—if pricing drops materially, the profitability thesis for model API businesses deteriorates significantly. The three frameworks (GPU leasing at 31% ROIC, proprietary model API at 46% ROIC, third-party model API at 25% ROIC) assume token pricing holds at $1-2.50 per million tokens. If pricing compresses to $1 or below per million tokens, base case becomes bear case.

Sentiment can suppress quality businesses for extended periods. Meta and Reddit are high-quality businesses with strong fundamentals, yet market sentiment remains negative. This creates opportunity but also requires patience and conviction.
